idea-plugin.name: Process Diary
idea-plugin.description:
See running processes, listening ports and CPU / memory / disk / network usage without leaving the IDE, and clean up the dev servers you forgot about.

  • Status bar widget with live CPU and memory; click for CPU, memory, disk and network graphs and the heaviest processes.
  • Process Diary tool window: list or tree view, search by name, PID, port or working directory, stable ordering, multi-select stop, and a detail panel that explains what a process is.
  • "This project" scope: only processes whose working directory is inside the current project.
  • Port conflicts: when a Run/Debug configuration fails with "port already in use" (Spring Boot, Node.js, Go, uvicorn, Rails, Java and more), see who holds the port and Stop it and rerun in one click.
  • Leftover processes: when a run stops but child or detached processes keep running, get a notification to stop them.
  • Java processes: see the main class or jar instead of just "java" (Gradle Daemon, Kotlin Daemon, your Spring Boot app), with Java heap usage.
  • Containers tab: Docker containers with published ports, CPU and memory; start, stop, restart and remove. When a run fails because a container holds the port, Stop container and rerun.
  • Usage alerts: get notified when CPU or memory stays high, with the processes using the most.
  • Find Action: "Stop Process Using Port…" and "Find Process by Port…" (assign shortcuts in Keymap).
  • Settings → Tools → Process Diary: refresh interval, status bar format, language (English / Korean), watchers.

Works on macOS, Windows and Linux. The UI is available in English and Korean (한국어).
